Paper 1 — General Studies (200 marks)

2 marks per correct answer, −⅓ of that (0.667) per wrong answer. Cut-offs are on Paper 1 only and come from published results; check the UPSC notice before relying on them. You can overwrite the target.

Paper 2 — CSAT (qualifying, 33%)

2.5 marks per correct answer, −⅓ (0.833) per wrong answer. You need 66 of 200 (33%). CSAT marks are not added to the Paper 1 rank.

What-if: questions you must get right for the target

Formula: minimum correct = (3×target + 2×attempted) ÷ 8. "Safe" adds a 10-mark buffer. One wrong answer costs 2.67 marks relative to leaving it blank.

Subject-wise projection

Enter how many questions you expect to attempt and get right in each subject. It adds up to a projected Paper 1 score against the target above.

Previous-year weightage by subject (2011–2025)

Enter the number of GS Paper 1 questions per subject for each year (each row should total 100). Values save in this browser. Paste a CSV (header: Year, then the subject names) to fill it quickly.
